title: LLM Observability, Evaluation, Experimentation Platform — Dat Ngo, Arize
talk_summary: Arize's Dat Ngo pitches observability, evals, and experimentation as the three pillars for making agents work, framed as 'software reimagined' with OpenTelemetry traces/spans as the audit substrate. The concrete mechanisms are span/session/trajectory-scoped evals, golden datasets to tune LLM judges, deterministic evals to avoid LLM cost, and exposing all primitives via CLI/tools so coding agents can drive the flywheel.

takeaways.technique: Scope evals by span vs session vs trajectory
takeaways.what_they_do: Classifies evals by scope: single span (one input/output), multi-span (data across components, e.g. how agents pass data), trajectory (did calls happen in the right order), and session (state machine: was user frustrated, all questions answered).
takeaways.evidence_quote: evals can be run on you can think a single kind of component. You know, we call that a span kind of eval

takeaways.what_they_do: Uses logic/schema checks (valid JSON, required non-null fields) as a cheap signal tier before spending LLM calls or human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't always have to use an LLM call or even humans. Determinism is super nice

takeaways.technique: Tune LLM judge against a golden dataset
takeaways.what_they_do: Labels a trusted golden set (domain expert quality column), then tunes the LLM-as-judge to approximate that human/expert signal rather than trusting the judge cold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm going to run my LLM as a judge on some, you know, golden data set so that you can tune your LLM as a judge

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly warns that every eval has a cost and teams should find the minimal set that tells them the app works as intended.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just because you can eval something doesn't mean you always should ... what are the minimal set of evals I can get away with

takeaways.technique: Expose platform primitives as CLI/tools for coding agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than requiring humans in dashboards, Arize exposes all observability/eval/experiment primitives via CLI plus tools and skills so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) can drive them programmatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We realize people are very comfortable with their cloud code and code X's. So we expose all the primitives via the CLI and and a set of tools and skills.

takeaways.technique: Trajectory eval to catch ordering/dependency bugs
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses trajectory evals to find root causes where components ran out of order (B before A when B depends on A) and then fixes by injecting context/instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I did B before A and actually B has a dependency on A ... we need to put some context in there
